overview: Black answers the Center Game with a counter-strike on d5. Most games go 3.dxe5 dxe4 4.Qxd8+ Kxd8 with an early queen trade where Black has lost castling but White has little extra, or 3.exd5 exd4 with an open centre. I am unsure of the exact move distribution, so the notes are general.

white_ideas.idea: Trade queens and exploit Black's lost castling rights.
Take on d5 and develop quickly with Nf3 and Bc4.

black_ideas.idea: Hold the e4 pawn and use the open d-file.
Develop rapidly and put the d4 pawn under pressure.

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after early exchanges, queens traded on d8.

character.notes: Early exchanges give a steady, simplified game in the main line.

gambit.notes: Material is level in the main exchanges.

soundness.notes: Probably sound for Black; the name gambit refers to a rarely tried pawn offer.

structure.notes: Open lines after pawn exchanges in the centre.

approach.notes: Rare reply that strong players seldom use.

level.notes: Not much theory; the endgame-like play needs understanding.
